answer: Require each identity to post a refundable bond bound to one verified device, as distinctive as a single opal. Before answering, the agent must complete a slow, device-bound proof-of-work task that takes real minutes on real hardware and cannot be replayed. A genuine agent pays once and tends its standing across a whole garden of challenges, while a Sybil farmer must buy separate hardware time and post a separate bond for every fake identity. In a tundra of cheap copies, that per-identity cost makes mass fakery unprofitable: copies stall on the work or lose bonds when juries spot duplication.
